notes: DOI 10.1046/j.1365-2958.2000.02212.x = PMID 11123678 (Fields & Hackstadt 2000, Mol Microbiol), title "Evidence for the secretion of Chlamydia trachomatis CopN by a type III secretion mechanism." Quote verbatim in abstract. Secretion documented: His-CopN secreted by Y. enterocolitica in Ca2+/pYV-dependent fashion; CopN secreted by chlamydiae to inclusion membrane. Organism C. trachomatis matches (serovar not specified, same species as D/UW-3/CX).

DOI 10.1128/IAI.73.7.4327-4337.2005 = PMID 15972527 (Kanack et al. 2005). Both quote sentences verbatim in abstract ("A SepZ-CyaA fusion was secreted and translocated into HeLa cells in a TTSS-dependent manner"; "we propose to rename SepZ as EspZ"). Ref is EPEC; row is EHEC O157:H7 Sakai - strain_diff, acceptable for conserved LEE effector. Documents T3SS translocation directly (CyaA fusion).

DOI 10.1073/pnas.0604891103 = PMID 16990433 / PMC1595455 (Tobe et al. 2006). Verified Table 1 "Summary of E. coli O157:H7 effectors" via PMC full text: EspJ (ECs2714, Sp14) listed in Effector column, confirmed by translocation (SC). Sakai strain = row organism. Quote is table-cell reference; table title and effector name verbatim.
Same ref/PMC1595455. Table 1 Effector column lists NleC (ECs0847, Sp3), confirmed by beta-lactamase fusion translocation (B). Sakai strain. Table title and effector name verbatim.

Same ref/PMC1595455. Table 1 lists NleG family (14 members, e.g. ECs1824 Sp9) in Effector column, confirmed by secretome+FLAG translocation (SF). Sakai strain. Largest effector family per abstract. Table title and effector name verbatim.
Same ref/PMC1595455. Table 1 lists EspL2 (ECs3855, SpLE3) in Effector column, confirmed by secretome+FLAG translocation (SF). Sakai strain. Table title and effector name verbatim.

DOI 10.1126/science.290.5496.1594 = PMID 11090361 (Orth et al. 2000, Science). Quote "Homologs of the Yersinia virulence effector YopJ are found in both plant and animal bacterial pathogens" verbatim in abstract. BUT this is a YopJ-as-cysteine-protease mechanism paper; quote calls YopJ a "virulence effector" via homology, does NOT document T3SS secretion/translocation (no supernatant/translocation assay in abstract). Ref organism Y. pseudotuberculosis vs row Y. pestis CO92 = strain_diff for conserved effector. YopJ/YopP is a well-established Yersinia T3SS effector elsewhere; flag for human review - cited quote/ref does not establish secretion under strict rubric.

DOI 10.1128/IAI.73.1.146-154.2005 = PMID 15618149 (Raffatellu et al. 2005). Quote verbatim in abstract ("T3SS-1 secreted proteins (effectors) SopE2 and SopB are required for invasion while the SipA protein accelerates entry into cells"). SipA named a T3SS-1 secreted effector. Organism S. Typhimurium matches (strain not LT2-specific in ref; SipA conserved). Documents SipA as T3SS-1 secreted effector.

DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0248975 = PMID 33735297 (Takemura et al. 2021). Quote "We also showed that PipA was secreted into RAW264.7 cells through T3SS-2." verbatim in abstract. Organism S. Typhimurium matches. Documents PipA secretion via T3SS-2 directly.

DOI 10.1128/JB.187.2.649-663.2005 = PMID 15629936 (Petnicki-Ocwieja et al. 2005). Quote verbatim in abstract ("Both HopB1 and HrpK were secreted in culture and translocated into plant cells via the TTSS. However, the translocation of HrpK required its C-terminal half."). Organism P. syringae pv. tomato DC3000 matches exactly. Documents HrpK secretion+translocation via TTSS.
